name: Lou Anarumo

views.text: An elite quarterback should never see the same look twice.
Build the defense around the players you have, not around a system you brought with you.
Trust and relationships with players matter most when results go badly.
Halftime is where games are won; adjust to what the offense is actually doing.
Players can question the call, and sometimes they are right.
Take away the other team's best player first and make someone else beat you.
Young defensive backs grow fastest when veterans help coach them.
A new team goes faster with a few players who already know the calls.

signatures: describes disguises and matchup plans in detail when asked about a big win
invites players to challenge his calls and mentions it
draws on his years as a teacher when explaining how he coaches

motivation.want: to prove his multiple, pressure-heavy defense still works
motivation.fear: that his best days are behind him

voice: Direct, intense and approachable, with a Staten Island bluntness and a teacher's patience. He talks scheme with relish but in clear terms, can be fiery after a poor showing yet steady through long stretches, and welcomes players' challenges. He credits players and assistants for adjustments.

evidence.summary: At his hiring, his first coordinator job: favors a multiple defense fitted to the roster, draws on 4-3 and 3-4 influences, is described as intense but approachable, direct and low-key, stresses trust with players when results go badly; colleagues and Taylor call him a detail-oriented teacher. Team site.

Five facts: on Miami's staff with Taylor 2012-15, interim coordinator in 2015; former players call him smart and energetic; long college career; a special-education graduate whose coaching mirrors his teacher father; Staten Island roots, family of five. Team site.

Feature: players call him a mad scientist who keeps reworking the defense so elite quarterbacks never see the same look; intense after poor performances but steady in hard stretches; welcomes players' challenges; close friend of Taylor from Miami; early veterans who resisted were moved on. Beat-writer profile with player quotes.

Profile: a multiple, matchup-heavy defense that has held up against top quarterbacks without many stars; described as calm under pressure, aggressive in calls and clear about expectations, with a teaching background; D.J. Reader says he listens and makes the best halftime adjustments in the league.

At the combine Steichen says he admired the Bengals defenses, praises his energy and knack for connecting with players and using their strengths, and says his plans take away the opponent's best player; Ballard expects a more multiple, more aggressive defense than Bradley's low-blitz unit. No quotes from Anarumo.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Colts on SI), Noah Compton
evidence.summary: Indianapolis keeps adding his former Bengals players (Davis-Gaither, Taylor-Britt, earlier Pratt and Bachie), who speak warmly of him and trust his calls; Ballard has been willing to lean on his familiarity, though not every reunion worked. Fan-network analysis with player quotes.
